scope.flow: User2 buys launchTokens from the launchpad via buy() after User1 has purchased 90% of BONDING_SUPPLY; remaining 10% is allocated via bonding curve and the contract attempts to swap the remaining tokens in _createPairAndSwapRemaining

statements.text: User1 has bought launchTokens equivalent to 90% of the BONDING_SUPPLY from the launchpad.
User2 attempts to buy launchTokens equivalent to 20% of the BONDING_SUPPLY from the launchpad.
User2 uses quoteQuoteForBase() in SimpleBondingCurve.sol to calculate the required quoteToken amount and sets slippage protection accordingly.
In buy() of launchpad.sol, since 90% of BONDING_SUPPLY launchTokens were already sold, the remaining 10% is allocated to User2 using the bonding curve.
Because total sold launchTokens reached BONDING_SUPPLY, the contract attempts to swap the remaining 10% and give it to User2 via _createPairAndSwapRemaining.

Although a slippage check is performed during the swap, if slippage occurs the function does not revert; instead it treats the swap as unsuccessful and returns the tokens, losing the intended slippage protection.
When a swap performed during User2's buy incurs slippage beyond the slippage protection set from quoteQuoteForBase(), the buy must revert rather than silently treat the swap as unsuccessful.
User2's buy of launchTokens equivalent to 20% of BONDING_SUPPLY should deliver the intended 20% amount at the price calculated via the bonding curve, not a reduced amount at a higher price.
After User2's buy, User2 should still be able to sell the acquired launchTokens; reaching BONDING_SUPPLY should not deactivate the launch such that selling is impossible.
User2 ends up receiving only 10% of the BONDING_SUPPLY (at a higher price than initially calculated) instead of the intended 20%.
This results in the loss of the intended slippage protection functionality.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether User2's buy transaction succeeds or reverts overall; only that the swap is treated as unsuccessful.
Report does not specify the exact slippage bound or numeric price values, only that the price is higher than initially calculated.
Report does not establish whether the swap failure is triggered by actual market slippage in a concrete observed transaction or is a conditional scenario.
Report does not state who may call buy() or any authorization condition; no unauthorized-caller claim is supported.
